title: Grades: Key Policies and Contacts (Pass/No Pass, Audit, Withdrawal)
text:
PASS/NO PASS (P/NP)
- P/NP is available only to students who officially elect it through registration. Instructors cannot assign it.
- P means C- or better for undergraduate letter-graded courses (B or better for graduate courses). NP means D+ or below (undergraduate) or B- or below (graduate). Neither affects GPA.
- Undergraduate rules: not available in courses numbered 390 or 490, in "WRIT-140 or 340," or to satisfy minor requirements. Up to 24 units may count toward a degree, and up to 4 of those may count toward General Education. Cannot fulfill major requirements unless the major department grants written permission through its exception process. Some departments may restrict which requirements P/NP courses can satisfy.
- Graduate rules: departmental approval is required; P/NP coursework cannot be applied toward a graduate degree.
- Deadline (both levels): P/NP can be elected only through the add-classes deadline. Course-specific dates are in the Schedule of Classes.
- The Spring 2027 Registration Calendar gives the session 001 deadline as Jan 29, 2027 (see the calendar page).

AUDIT (V)
- Lets a student attend a course without grades or credit. Audited courses do not appear on the transcript or grade reports.
- Must be elected during registration, by the end of the third week of classes (or the equivalent for shorter courses), via Web Registration or in-person registration.
- Not available in courses numbered 390, 490, 590, 594, 690, 790, 794, 990 or 994.

OTHER GRADE OPTIONS
- Letter-Graded: the standard option for courses approved as letter-graded.
- Credit/No Credit (CR/NC): for courses that may only be graded CR/NC. CR and NC do not affect GPA.
- In Progress (IP): for courses that exceed one semester.
- Withdrawal (W): available after the refund deadline and before the withdrawal deadline. Only a W may be assigned. Instructors cannot withdraw students.

DROP AND WITHDRAWAL DEADLINES
- Courses dropped by the end of week 3 do not appear on the transcript.
- Courses dropped from week 4 through week 12 receive a W.
- No course may be dropped after week 12, though petitions are rarely approved.
- Students cannot withdraw from a course where an academic integrity violation has been committed or alleged.

OTHER MARKS
- UW: assigned when a student stops attending before the week 12 deadline without officially withdrawing. Counts as zero grade points.
- Incomplete (IN): assigned for documented illness or emergency after week 12. Must be completed within one calendar year, or it becomes IX (expired incomplete), counted as zero grade points.

CONTACTS
